title: Coroner's inquest to examine the violent death of Westside man
article: A four-day coroner's inquest has been scheduled to probe the facts surrounding the passing of a man who died in Westside RCMP custody last June.
On June 7, 2006, RCMP were called to a Glenrosa neighbourhood to deal with a man involved in a violent domestic dispute with his parents.
When officers arrived, RCMP say, the man took on officers and seemed to possess "super-human" strength.
Eventually, five officers managed to subdue 38-year-old Derrick Patrick Madrusan and bound his hands behind his back and used bracelets on his legs before placing him in a police cruiser.
After being left alone for "moments," officers found him unresponsive in the vehicle.
Paramedics, who had been tending to Madrusan's parents, then turned their attention to the 38-year-old.
Despite their efforts, Madrusan was declared dead upon arrival to Kelowna General Hospital.
At the inquest, presiding coroner Bruce Chamberlayne and a five- person jury will publicly hear evidence from subpoeaned witnesses in order to determine the facts surrounding the death.
The jury will also have the opportunity to make recommendations aimed at preventing deaths under similar circumstances in the future, the coroner's service says in a press release.
The coroner's service is an independent fact-finding agency that may not make any finding of legal responsibility, they note.
The four day inquest is scheduled to get underway on Nov. 13.
